triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The refundable Oregon EITC was gated only on full-year residency plus a valid input domain rather than on the module's bounded no-held-branch profile, so on profiles the module explicitly holds as unsupported it published a nonzero credit (e.g. 170) while every other output in the same pipeline returned 0, asserting a net Oregon result the encoding has no source support for instead of failing closed.
triage.triage_notes: Only one module file in the commit (chunk covers index 0 as expected); the commit also touched the companion test file and the signed encoding manifest (hash/signature bookkeeping only). Diff is a one-line gate swap at rules[or_pit_2026_profile_candidate_refundable_earned_income_credit].versions[0].formula; every sibling candidate rule in the file (deduction, schedule tax, nonrefundable credits, bounded net liability) was already gated on or_pit_2026_bounded_profile_applies, so this was the single fail-open output. Test evidence: `sb1507_eitc_young_dependent_rate_17_percent` (federal EITC 1000, dependent under three) changed its expected EITC from '170' to '0' while asserting `or_pit_2026_dependent_exemption_source_hold_applies: holds` and `or_pit_2026_bounded_profile_applies: not_holds`; two held-path tests gained ~19 zero assertions each. DOUBT worth a reviewer's attention: I read the cited provision (ORS 315.266 as amended by SB 1507 sec. 3, via resolve_provision on us-or/statute/session-laws/2026/sb1507/document-1) and it allows the credit to 'an eligible resident individual' at 14 percent (17 percent 'for a taxpayer with a dependent under the age of three at the close of the tax year') with no bounded-profile condition, so the pre-fix 170 was statutorily plausible for that taxpayer. The wrongness is therefore against the module's own declared hold architecture and fail-closed convention (an ungrounded partial legal result) rather than against the statute's numeric rule; a reviewer may prefer classification 'unclear', or kind 'wrong_entity_or_scope' (output surface / supported population) over 'polarity_or_logic'. I chose polarity_or_logic because the task taxonomy names 'fail-open vs fail-closed' under it and the commit subject is literally 'Fail close Oregon 2026 held tax outputs'. Side effect to note: because `or_pit_2026_has_dependent_under_age_three_at_year_end` is itself a disjunct of `or_pit_2026_dependent_exemption_source_hold_applies`, the statutory 17 percent young-dependent branch inside the EITC formula is now unreachable in this module, and the test still named `sb1507_eitc_young_dependent_rate_17_percent` now asserts 0. The commit is a repair round inside PR #1038 (merged 2026-07-24); the commit message body is empty, so all stated reasoning comes from the PR body's 'Review-fix cycle' section; PR has no separate review or comment records in the bundle.
triage.verifier_justification: The one-hunk diff replaces the gate on the public refundable Oregon EITC candidate from the weak pair `or_pit_2026_is_full_year_resident and or_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid` with the module's declared boundary `or_pit_2026_bounded_profile_applies`, so a branch that previously fired on profiles the module holds as unsupported now fails closed; the companion test flips that exact case from '170' to '0' and adds 19 zero assertions on the invalid and new-jobs-held paths. This is a genuine change of encoded meaning, not bookkeeping, and it is the single odd-one-out rule: the pre-fix file already referenced `bounded_profile_applies` in 20 places (every other profile_candidate / bounded money output), the post-fix file in 21. Fail-open versus fail-closed is named explicitly under polarity_or_logic, and the gate substitution is a mis-combined boolean condition rather than an amount, boundary, date, or missing clause, so the first reader's kind holds. I tried the two available refutations and neither displaces it: wrong_entity_or_scope (output surface) is the runner-up but describes the consequence rather than the mechanism, and not_a_defect is weakened by the fact that the pre-fix rule contradicted the module's own documented hold contract even though the 14/17 percent value it produced was itself source-correct.

triage.verifier_notes: Caveat a reviewer should weigh: I read ORS 315.266 as amended by SB 1507 sec. 3 through the pinned release (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, provision text sha256 29a0174648242146a78c2ab2dbf04b615bb00016f6a0ee18027da9ffee2fd895). It allows "an eligi- ble resident individual ... a credit ... equal to [nine] 14 percent of the earned income credit allowable", with 17 percent for a dependent under three, and conditions nothing on the module's held branches (new-jobs credit, dependent-exemption hold, kicker, PTE-E, held modifications). So on a held profile the statute's own answer is still 14/17 percent of federal EITC; the post-fix 0 is the encoding's hold convention, not a literal source value, and the pre-fix gate actually tracked the statute's resident condition. The wrongness is against the module's declared bounded contract (all sibling money outputs return 0 when the profile is held) rather than against the words of ORS 315.266 — reviewers who require source-text disagreement for "fidelity" could argue not_a_defect here. The concrete hazard that makes it a real defect: with tax-after-nonrefundable-credits already zeroed on a held profile, an ungated EITC of 170 lets a consumer derive a -170 Oregon refund the module cannot support. Two more context points: the reader's phrase "asserting a net Oregon result" is slightly off, since `or_pit_2026_bounded_net_income_tax_liability_candidate` was already gated on the bounded profile and returned 0 pre-fix; and this commit is an intra-PR repair inside PR #1038, the same PR that first encoded the module, so the defect never landed on main independently (relevant only if the corpus policy excludes intra-PR review repairs).
